OwnerName: Dutch Girl Holdings LLC & Irving Ventures LLC
Leslie A Amestoy, Pierre Jean Amestoy Jr & Roger K Beasley
Jacob M Pegram & Timothy A Pegram
Glen Hill Farm, Little Red Feather Racing & Madaket Stables

Spotlight: 14,000euros yearling; 60,000euros breeze-up buy in May; second foal; Kodi Bear half-brother to Italian 7f 2yo winner; dam useful 6f winner; could go well on debut.
By speedy juvenile Ubettabelieveit; dropped away to finish 17l last of 11 on Thirsk debut ten days ago (6f, good; 50-1); major improvement clearly needed.

By No Nay Never; has finished a clear second in a Pontefract maiden (5f, good to firm) and a 6f Ripon novice (good); wore a tongue-tie on both occasions but that is now discarded; an obvious candidate but he drops to a sharp 5f from 6f.

OwnerName: Mpr, A & Glo Outlaw & K Quinn
Spotlight: Fair second in four-runner maiden on Carlisle debut (5f, good) but beaten over 6l when last of five at Ripon (5f, good) since; needs to bounce back.
Fairly exposed now and was behind The Mean Fiddler at Pontefract (5f, good) two runs ago; has a bit to find with an official mark of 67.
Filly by Advertise; showed a little promise when over 5l fifth of six on her Beverley debut 11 days ago; should improve for that run.
Weakened to finish nearly 10l last of eight on her debut at Ayr ten days ago (6f, good to soft; 50-1); may do better at 5f but improvement needed.
Didn't look straightforward when tailed off last of eight on her 5f debut at Catterick (33-1) in June; hood now tried; best watched for now.

Back on his last successful mark (AW) and wins at Epsom and Chepstow (both on good ground) last summer suggest today's course should be fine; won't mind the return to 5f, either, having been pestered in front last time, and is one to consider.

Running consistently all season and the handicapper continues to give him every chance (5lb lower than when last successful); ran well on his only previous start here too but he's ultimately made a career of getting beaten at short prices.

In-form front-runner who has two wins, a second and two thirds to his name in five runs here; on career-high mark, though, having been put up 5lb for his Newmarket win early in the month under 7lb claimer Chloe Lyons.

Back to something like his best since the hood came off for this yard, winning twice this summer and going back up a stone in the weights; another solid effort off this mark in an apprentice handicap at Windsor last Monday and looks set to go well once more.

Notched a third win over C&D earlier in the month; that race rather fell into his lap, though, with the leaders going off too hard, and he'll find today's company tougher off a 6lb higher mark; not disgraced, having made late headway, here (6f) on Sunday.

Consistent and likes it here; 7lb better off with Secret Handsheikh than when second to him over C&D earlier in the month but he's spent most of his career running in lesser company and currently is weighted to his best; faded late over 6f here on Sunday.
Showed improvement to score at the sixth attempt in a Wolverhampton maiden (7f, AW) last Monday in a first-time hood (retained); steps up to 1m on nursery debut and holds sound claims.

Showed ability when 7l third in a York novice (7f, good to firm) on second start but beaten over 18l by the same rival in a similar contest at Ripon (1m, good) nine days ago; dons first-time cheekpieces on nursery debut and may well show more.

Off the mark at this track (7f, good) last month; never recovered from a slow start when fourth of five in a selling nursery back here ((7f, good) 17 days ago; at least she has a win under her belt now up in trip but others may be more progressive.
Has shown only modest form in three contests; steps up in trip on nursery debut and market will be best guide.
Hasn't finished closer to the winner than her debut fifth in a Chester seller (7f, good to soft; beaten about 3l) in June; steps up in trip but hard to fancy in her third nursery.

First sign of ability when fifth in a Hamilton maiden (5f, good to soft) in June; gelded subsequently; well held when beaten 16l on nursery debut at Leicester (7f, good to firm) last month but steps up in trip and may be worth another chance.
Has shown little in three runs at about 7f but she's well bred and from a leading yard so significant improvement could easily be on the cards now moving into a nursery.

RaceName: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-brother to three winners, two of whom went close on 2yo debut (one for this yard, which boasts a much better record with 2yos on the AW than turf, including this season); holds a sales-race entry next month and the market will guide.

RaceName: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Yard far from known for juveniles (0-19 this season), especially first time, but this 45,000euros breeze-up 2yo offered a bit of promise behind the two market leaders on recent Windsor debut; entitled to improve.

RaceName: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Best effort yet on his nursery debut at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) early in the month; was allowed his own way in front against the favoured rail that night but he sets the standard on that back in a maiden.

RaceName: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Best of the rest when some way off a couple of useful-looking 2yos on his Newmarket debut (6f, good to firm) recently; hard to know the merit of that as yet but he sat last for a long way in a messy affair and this is somewhat easier.

RaceName: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Started 66-1 and ran as the market predicted on her Newmarket debut a few weeks ago; she'll need to take a big forward step.
Comes here in decent form having won at Ripon in June and finished a close second to a stablemate there last month (also 1m2f, good); contender.

Usually a front-runner; doesn't have the best of strike-rates (2-22) but three good runs in blinkers  at Ayr (1m; all on good to firm; has form on good to soft) in June and he stays this trip; a possible.
Three good runs since the tongue-tie went on, last time finishing third of five at Nottingham (8.5f, good to firm); each-way chance.
Three wins over 1m4f here, the latest off 4lb higher last August (good) when with Dianne Sayer; tailed off over 1m5f here last time (slowly away); takes a significant drop in trip; cheekpieces tried.

Three Flat wins, latest off 7lb higher at Wetherby in June 2025 (1m2f, good to firm); well beaten on first two runs (following a break) this term, but shaped better on AW latest (1m3f); still has a bit to prove at present.
Both wins on this track, the latest over C&D off this mark in first-time cheekpieces in June (good); hasn't done as well since, but an interesting contender on a track where his record is 2131.
Two wins last season, the second over C&D last August off this mark; runner-up on his last three starts, beaten 1.25l by a previous winner over C&D last time; contender.
Record of 3-33 on turf; good third at Doncaster in July (1m, good to firm) but well beaten last time (1m2f, good to firm); lacks consistency.

13-race maiden; beaten less than 2l when fourth at Ayr last time (1m2f, good to soft; second run after wind op); fair run in first-time cheekpieces in June and they are tried for the second time; each-way chance.
C&D winner off 7lb higher in August 2024; mixed form since but sound run when third over C&D  (good; second run after wind op, first with a tongue-tie) 17 days ago; has a chance on that run.

OwnerName: Brian Ellison Racing Club & M Dale
Spotlight: Lightly raced in recent seasons and hasn't shown his best form since returning from a long break this term; 5lb out of the handicap; others appeal more.

Has gone close on turf but his five wins, including four for this yard, have come on the AW; a 4lb penalty for last Tuesday's Lingfield Polytrack win, back in the blinkers, leaves little room for manoeuvre.
Dual firm-ground Bath winner this season, latterly off 3lb lower for Owen Lewis late last month; as high in the weights now as he's been for a few years and his record round here is nothing exciting.
Generally in good form since cheekpieces went on but she's been costing herself with slow starts lately; won't mind coming back up from 5f and much will hinge on how she gets on at the stalls.

Progressive in the first half of last year for George Boughey before being sold for 21,000gns in the autumn; has struggled in Ireland this year but was well backed last time and the booking of Billy Loughnane draws the eye with first-time visor added.

Dual soft-ground winner, latterly over C&D last autumn off an 8lb higher mark; has been running over 7f in recent times and the question is whether he still has the toe for this trip under today's conditions.
Cheekpieces had a positive early impact during a good spell for her yard last month but she's been below par as favourite the past twice; much will depend on the effect of a new form of headgear.
Unexposed; won 7f Newcastle novice in June having previously finished runner-up in a 6f maiden at Pontefract (good to soft); not so good on handicap debut last time (AW) but not out of it.

OwnerName: N Bradley 29, Resdev & South Bank Racing
Spotlight: Completed a hat-trick on final three starts last term, the first in a 7f seller here (good), the last two in handicaps on heavy ground; mainly in good form this season and could go well on return from a break.

Unexposed; won a 6f Catterick novice in June (good to soft); two fair runs since, including second on handicap debut at Catterick last time (6f, good to firm); should be capable of better but was below par on only previous run at 7f (debut).

OwnerName: Alfa Site Services Ltd & Graeme Curnow
Spotlight: Won a C&D maiden on reappearance in May (good); two sound runs since, latest a short-head second to a subsequent easy winner in a 7f Kempton handicap; up 3lb; chance.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Down the field in a 6f Goodwood handicap last time; in good form earlier in the season with two wins in 7f fillies' handicaps at Catterick; a possible.

Won a 5f AW maiden for Ed Bethell last September; two fair runs in 6f turf handicaps on first two starts this term (with a hood on second occasion); tried in cheekpieces last time (met trouble); now up in trip with a hood back on.
Won 7f handicap at Catterick off 2lb lower in July (good to firm); bit disappointing last two starts (over 1m/7.5f); may fare better back down in trip.
Won 6f Newcastle novice for Ed Bethell last December; well beaten all three starts in handicaps for new yard this year, including on first try at 7f last time; on a good mark but a bit to prove.
Ex-Irish; sound efforts when placed in two handicaps at Ayr in July (7f/1m, good/good to firm); below par on softer ground last time; could bounce back.
Placed three times, all on the AW, from four starts last season; hasn't progressed this year; well handicapped but others appeal more.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Goodwood novice winner for James Horton last spring who tumbled down the weights in Ireland this season; solid in the market for her new yard at Newmarket on Friday and that was a step back in the right direction.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Goodwood/Lingfield winner who's been running well all summer without looking to have anything in hand off this mark, latterly when splitting a couple of subsequent winners over C&D early last month; looks set to go well again.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Decent 3yo who's enjoyed a revival round Chepstow of late, beating a subsequent winner off 7lb lower last month before following up a fortnight ago; every chance of completing the hat-trick.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Keen-going front-runner who landed a second Epsom victory (also a C&D winner) when showing the right attitude to get back up late last month; won back-to-back races last summer and no surprise to see history repeat itself upped a fair 2lb.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Wildly inconsistent mare who was hit with a sharp rise for an easy Leopardstown win in April; twice well held at the same course since for an Irish trainer who has also declared Blue Anthem in the 3:30

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Made it 3-3 over C&D with two wins for Tom Queally, who's back up today, in June; didn't look to see out 1m4f in better company here last time, when hanging left as usual; this is more his level.

RaceName: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap
Spotlight: Resumed from a layoff in good nick, her stamina carrying the day over 1m on comeback before a solid effort off her revised mark over C&D last time; one to consider under Billy Loughnane in first-time headgear.

Landed her fifth win in a Beverley handicap (5f, good to firm) last month; had excuses subsequently but never showed back there 11 days ago; drops back in class and is on her last winning mark so may well show more.
Doesn't win very often but had her day in the sun when making all over C&D in June off 4lb lower; largely consistent since but win record of 1-20 on turf is offputting.
Has claims on his short-head defeat over C&D (good) in June off this mark but has failed to back up that run twice since; usual headgear left off here.

He's won six times and has been runner-up in his last three contests, latest when jockey dropped her whip when in front inside the final furlong at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm); he may well gain compensation today.
Has been a grand servant to the yard with two of his nine wins coming over C&D; latest success came at Ayr (5f, good to firm) last month and he should not be far away.
0-9 but has shown enough to suggest her turn is not far off; closest when beaten 1l at Catterick (5f, good to firm) this month.
Two of his three wins have been over C&D but losing run is mounting up; first-time tongue-tie could do with having a positive effect.
Her last three wins have all been over C&D but she hasn't been firing recently; the return to this track for the first time this year needs to have an impact.
Has made the frame in four of her last six starts; just needs to show a little more to get involved.
Eight-race maiden who has been well held since his debut fifth at Doncaster last July; makes stable debut but others have stronger claims.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Won C&D maiden in October 2024 for Hughie Morrison but has struggled in handicaps since; the switch to current yard has not changed his fortunes and he's showing little sign that he is ready to take advantage of a declining mark.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Just 1-26 and that was on AW in 2024; has yet to be placed from five runs on turf and his turn is more likely to come when back on AW.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Five-time winner (5f-7f) when based in Ireland; below form in two runs for current stable and his stamina for 1m is still unproven after fading over C&D 18 days ago (went off fast).

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Course specialist who landed his sixth win on this track earlier this month, in a C&D classified; beaten at odds-on over 7f here 24 hours later but will be more at home back over 1m and must be on the shortlist.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Three 7f wins at this track but has also won at 1m; resumed winning ways in a classified at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) ten days ago but back up 5lb and will find it tougher back in a handicap.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Just 1-20, her sole success coming at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last December; beaten in a classified on Tuesday and needs to get back on track.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: 0-9 when trained by Jack Channon; shaped encouragingly when staying on to finish fifth of nine behind River Wharfe over C&D (good to firm) 19 days ago on reappearance and stable debut and may finish closer this time.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: Sole success came in a classified at Lingfield (1m, AW) in January; hasn't matched that form since and needs to do better; on career-low mark.

RaceName: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap
Spotlight: His only win since 2023 came in a classified at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in January; has made the frame in four of his last five starts and holds place claims.

Maiden who's gone sharply the wrong way for this yard, running poorly in three starts this season; didn't look to see out 1m2f (soft) two months ago and this is easier again but she's hard to recommend.

Dual Ripon winner last summer who's regressed and run below market expectations on last two starts; this is easier off a career-low mark (9lb lower than when last successful) but he could have done without the recent rain.

Combination of a first-time visor and drop to 0-50 classified company enough to see her end a losing run a fortnight ago; win last August came off a stone-higher mark and she's shortlisted now back in the groove.
Generally struggled this season and the years look to be catching up now; an easy 1m such as this would have been a bare minimum even in his pomp and Thats My Boy Luke may be his yard's best chance.

Just a single win to her name but showed more on her first crack at this trip at Ayr a fortnight ago, when going off hard in front and only letting Hostelry past; 4lb better off with that one today and this course should suit her style; player.

OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: C&D winner in June who didn't quite see it out over 1m1f here last time; not the easiest and often misses the break but a big field at this slightly lower level looks ideal; one to consider.

Regressive maiden who was going beyond 6f for the first time when said to have hung right throughout in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Ayr a fortnight ago (7f); hard to make a case, with Approaching Dawn looking his trainer's best shout.
Winless since 2yo days; competitive at this sort of level all summer but a couple of costly defeats here latterly (7f) and needs to find more.
Regressive maiden for two previous yards who ran poorly for his current trainer a few months ago on his return from almost a year off; since been gelded and doesn't make obvious appeal.

Sole win came at Ayr; among the market leaders back there early last month on first crack at 0-50 company, but finished well held behind Approaching Dawn; given a second go in a visor today, switched from cheekpieces.
Dual 7f winner who's pulled hard and not seen it out in three previous tries over this trip; shown very little in five runs for his current yard in any case.

Poor in five runs for Jack Channon, finishing tailed off on her sole start last year; entitled to have needed her recent comeback for her new trainer, who also saddles Caledonian Dream, but didn't show enough to warrant serious consideration today.

Fair 2yo for George Scott but generally struggled for his current trainer; brought over from Ireland twice early in the year (AW), when unplaced each time, and is some way down the pecking order back from a break.
Finished in the frame in three of five point starts; respectable fifth in 2m2f Galway bumper on rules debut; should strip fitter for that and bred to make a jumper; place chance.

Placed in one of two point-to-points; again placed in a Punchestown bumper in May (2m, good); showed an aptitude for hurdling when an 8.5l second in a maiden at the same venue (16.5f, good) and the winner Lizzie Twigg has won twice since; this longer trip should suit and leading claims if ready after break.
No joy in points and not much encouragement to take from heavy defeats at big odds in a bumper and two maiden hurdles; seems safe to rule out.
No impact in points or in first three starts over hurdles; hood needs to transform.

0-6 over hurdles; fell at the second-last when holding every chance in a Cork maiden hurdle last month (17.5f, good); easy to forgive latest effort in the Tribes at Galway; cheekpieces worn that day are left off; rated 113 and obvious chance.

Getaway gelding; closely related to bumper/2m4f hurdle winner Delta Run, half-brother to winners Theclockisticking (useful 2m-3m hurdle/chase) and Clay Pigeons (point/bumper/1m7f hurdle); dam unraced sister to Synchronised; appeal on paper and yard in form; check the market.
Unlikely winner based on tame efforts at huge odds here and at Tramore.
Pulled up in all three starts over hurdles; impossible to make a case for.
Pulled up in both points and beaten 112l in a Downpatrick bumper; can only be watched on hurdling debut.
Beaten a cumulative distance of 126l in maiden hurdles at Kilbeggan and Tramore; may do better when tackling handicaps.
Choeur Du Nord gelding; dam French 2m4f chase winner, half-sister to 2m4f hurdle/chase winner Hold Up La Colmine (by Choeur Du Nord), out of French 2m1f hurdle winner; check the market.
Elusive Pimpernel mare; dam unraced half-sister to Swedish Derby winner Moe Green out of unraced sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Scribe and 1m2f Listed winner Northern Hal; likely best watched.
Heavy defeat in a bumper and no impact in two starts over hurdles at huge odds; look elsewhere.
No impact in two points and tailed off at 100-1 on hurdles debut at Killarney; others preferred.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time course winner who remains consistent despite his age; recent strike-rate isn't great but he's down to 0-55 for the first time since returned to turf and Billy Loughnane is an obvious plus.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: C&D win last August came off 4lb higher but she's struggled since returned to turf, including back here earlier this month; hard to back her with conviction currently.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Always been best on the AW but off the mark on turf in a 0-50 classified event ten days ago; did a lot of racing over this trip in the past but does seem more effective over 6f these days and history suggests he's no good thing to back up Yarmouth.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Beaten-favourite in five of his last six starts, latterly behind Thanks Dad at Yarmouth, and has tended to pull hard/not see it out in a few starts at beyond sprint trips; capable off this mark but is still a maiden and comes with risks attached.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Appreciated the step back up from 6f when finally off the mark over C&D earlier this month; showed the right attitude that day for Mikkel Mortensen and it will only have boosted confidence; one to consider upped a fair 2lb.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Nursery win last backend (Tapeta) came in first-time cheekpieces; maybe the switch to first-time blinkers will do the job but it's hard to find any other positives, with him struggling this year and having stamina to prove.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices and well held in six runs for three yards; didn't see out 1m last time and it's too soon to put a line through her but would want to see some support before considering her.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Almost got up at Yarmouth last time (weak 0-50 classified event); more on her plate back into handicap company in first-time headgear but it's still early days with her.

RaceName: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap
Spotlight: Well-related filly who wasn't entirely without hope for James Ferguson, ignoring a poor one last month; new trainer has done the trick so many times with new recruits that she'd have to be considered in first-time headgear should the market speak her way.

RaceName: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 17-2, shaped encouragingly when fifth of nine in 7f Kempton novice on her debut for Ed Walker last September; off since but this daughter of Hello Youmzain can't be ruled out now starting out with another leading yard.

RaceName: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has shown fair form to make the frame in 6f Nottingham maiden and 7f Doncaster novice this summer, runner-up in four-runner event on latter occasion; likely needs to take a step forward to gain a first win here though.

RaceName: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 100-1 but took a big step forward with second of seven in 6f Salisbury novice 12 days ago; needs to back it up now.

RaceName: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 3,000gns 3yo; dam, 7f/1m winner (RPR 93), is a half-sister to useful winners Positive Impact (7f/1m) and Turntable (1m-1m2f); the market can guide for this Pinatubo filly on her first run.

RaceName: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Frankel filly who made a promising start with third of 11 in 6f maiden at Newbury 12 months ago; absent subsequently but remains with potential and a likely key player.

Has got his act together over hurdles; made all in a 17.5f maiden hurdle at Sligo (good) and followed up in a novice hurdle over this C&D (good); posted another solid effort in a 2m2f novice hurdle at Sligo on latest; obvious chance in first handicap with rider taking off 7lb.

In excellent form since return from a break, winning successive handicaps at Kilbeggan (2m3f, good) by 12l and at Cork (2m2f, good) by 8l; has gone up a total of 23lb and this is a tougher race but there could be more to come.

Won off 8lb lower at Cork in April (2m, yielding); back to form with solid 2.25l fourth of 14 here over 16.5f (good) on latest; has weakened late on both previous starts at this sort of trip so stamina a concern.
Flat winner is 0-5 over hurdles; showed a glimmer of promise when fifth in a Galway novice but beat just one rival home on handicap debut at Sligo five days ago; others make more appeal.

Gained breakthrough win in decisive fashion at Wexford last month (2m4f, good); raised 6lb and came up short in follow-up bid over the same C&D; this is a stronger race so work to do off the same mark.

Struggled badly on heavy ground earlier this year but has shown improved form on good ground in maiden hurdles at Wexford and Sligo since returning from a break; not obviously well treated and this looks a tough race in which to make his handicap debut.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Looked an excellent prospect when overcoming inexperience to make a winning debut in novice at Epsom (7f, good to firm) last month, forging clear last 1f; this son of Masar holds a Group 1 Dewhurst entry and is very much the one to beat despite conceding weight all round.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 42,000gns yearling; half-brother to 1m2f winner Guesstimate (RPR 78); dam, unplaced over 1m-11.6f (RPR 65), is a sister to useful winners Evaluation (1m6f-2m Flat and 2m hurdle) and Calculation (1m2f-14.5f), out of Gold Cup winner Estimate; this Australia colt needs considering on debut, especially if the market vibes are positive.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Blue Point colt who took a step forward from his debut when third of five in 7f Brighton novice 18 days ago; he can do better still but likely needs to here.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 35,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Sassi Neri (1m4f AW; RPR 73) and Tax Holiday (US 1m turf); dam, placed over 1m2f-1m4f (RPR 68), is a half-sister to Group 1 winners Japan (1m2f/1m4f) and Mogul (1m4f) and 1m2f Group 2 winner Secret Gesture; this son of Saxon Warrior can't be ruled out on his first start.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Built on debut with sixth of nine in 7f Epsom novice 25 days ago; this son of Without Parole needs to take another step forward now.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 16-1, hinted at promise with debut fifth of nine in novice at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) 22 days ago, keeping on late; more can be expected from this son of Bayside Boy over this longer trip.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Improved on his initial fifth with third of four in 7f Doncaster novice nine days ago; he may do better still but yard also has Camarda Rc in here.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 21,000gns foal; Sergei Prokofiev colt; half-brother to Group-placed 5f winner Show Me Show Me (RPR 100); dam, Hungarian 7f-1m winner, is a half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Too Cool For School; a noteworthy newcomer.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Well held in maidens at Leicester (7f) and Southwell (1m) this summer; significantly more is required from this Land Force colt.

RaceName: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Torquator Tasso colt who was much improved from his debut when a nose second of nine in 7f AW Lingfield maiden last month; strong at the finish there so he can go very well now stepping up to 1m.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Well held under her penalty at Killarney after winning a bumper at Roscommon; plenty of winning hurdlers further back in her pedigree, but stable second string and again penalised for this jumps debut.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Half-sister to smart hurdler Altobelli; good level of bumper form in four well spread-out appearances; 5/6 fav, looked paceless on hurdling debut over 2m3f at Downpatrick where she missed at the last two obstacles; trip likely to suit and yard in much better form now.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Her Sligo second was in a modest restricted maiden; only rated 90 and likely to struggle, although this longer trip may help.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Point winner was third of 22 in decent Navan maiden hurdle last November; tongue-tied, filled same spot behind useful winner over 2m2f at Downpatrick last month, where she couldn't lie up but came home well up the hill; this trip might suit.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Policy Maker newcomer out of maiden pointer; family of smart jumper Atone; best watched.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Big prices and poor form, including when tried in headgear last time.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest maiden pointer and well beaten in a maiden hurdle and a bumper.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Tailed off in a bumper; keen on hurdling debut at Sligo where well-beaten fourth over 2m2f.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: French import was fourth on only hurdles start; then ran in six chases, placing twice including when second over this trip; not seen since a fall in November; a dark one and the market will tell plenty; tongue-tied all starts.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ocavango 6yo is from a family with which the yard has done very well; only beaten 3l on hurdling debut at Killarney last October (winner rated 102); betting suggested she'd need Wexford comeback and steps up in trip now.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Daughter of Kew Gardens out of unraced half-sister to modest winning jumper; third in good-ground point in May.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Daughter of Westerner out of 2m-2m1f hurdle/chase winner; well beaten in two bumpers.

RaceName: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Third to a smart winner in 2m1f academy hurdle at Cork last October; not as good in similar contest following month; made the running when fourth to Goodgollymissholly in Roscommon bumper last month; fitter for that and tongue-tie goes on; chance if longer trip suits.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: In winning form on the AW at Wolverhampton (1m4f) in the winter but failed to beat a rival on his return from five months in 1m4f handicap at Newmarket last month; has something to prove now.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Signed off for David O'Meara with 1m4f handicap success at Ripon in June; changed hands for 36,000gns subsequently and not out of things for his new yard with tongue-tie added.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Fair 1m2f winner in France for Andre Fabre; not discredited when in the frame in 1m2f handicaps at Sandown and Lingfield for his new yard this summer; can't be dismissed.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Lingfield (1m2f) in May and backed it up with a good second of five at Sandown (1m2f) following month; must enter calculations after a break.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: On a losing run but he's proving consistent this season and posted a solid third of six in 1m2f handicap here two weeks ago; this course winner ought to be thereabouts once more.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Steadily progressing in handicaps and he comfortably gained a first success in five-runner event at Brighton (1m2f) 18 days ago; not taken lightly despite a 6lb weights hike.

RaceName: Play The Free £20,000 Matchbook Match 6 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Landed 11.5f novice at Lingfield in June; ran well in first-time cheekpieces when second of nine in 1m2f handicap at Chester 22 days ago; can race off a 1lb lower mark here so bold showing is on the cards in retained headgear.
Has finished remote third in all three maiden hurdles at 20.5f-24.5f on good ground; with shrewd yard so needs monitoring in the market on handicap debut.

OwnerName: J R Robinson & Mrs E Keane
Spotlight: Was off the track for almost three years but a respectable fourth over C&D last month proved he still retained ability; would probably prefer softer ground, however.
Left behind previous two modest runs to finish a 2.25l second of 13 at Wexford (3m, good) in first-time blinkers (retained); should be in the mix if the headgear works again.

Last won over hurdles here (2m1f, yld-sft) in August 2024; went close over C&D off 6lb higher in April 2025; below that level in just three runs since, including when beaten 26l here on latest (16.5f, good); needs a revival.
Flat winner showed little in maiden hurdles and similar story on handicap debut at Killarney when he never travelled; eased 2lb and blinkers now tried.

Won at Listowel (23.5f, good) off 5lb lower in May last year; subsequently went close off revised mark at Punchestown (3m, gd-yld) and Galway (3m, yielding) and is now 5lb lower than when beaten 1l in the latter race; positive signs at Wexford latest and enters calculations now.

Back from a spell chasing with a solid effort at Downpatrick (2m6f, good), beaten just 1.25l into second of 10; nudged up 2lb, so remains 8lb above sole success, but yard red hot so should be on the premises again.

Three wins over hurdles at this venue including over C&D; however, has failed to fire so far this year and was beaten 15l on latest over C&D (good); however, is now 3lb below her last winning mark so can't be written off.
Yet to show winning potential and struggled on handicap debut at Wexford 17 days ago; hood goes on.
On long losing run but did run into third over C&D on his penultimate start; not at his best here two weeks ago, however, so needs to bounce back.

Point-to-point winner hasn't cut much ice in maiden hurdles at 2m4f-3m on varying ground; hood worn the last twice is left off and rider booking a plus but will surely need this after mammoth absence.
Maiden shaped like he'd improve plenty for the run when a respectable 11.5l fifth of 16 over C&D, under a positive ride, on his return from a break two weeks ago; interesting.
AW Flat winner extended his record over hurdles to 0-7 when beaten 40l at Downpatrick earlier this month; not a bad run on the level at Tramore since but much more needed back over timber.
Off the mark over hurdles at Wexford on latest (3m, good), showing a willing attitude to score by a neck; 4lb rise for that seems fair but not sure this drop back in trip will suit.
Very modest form so far in maiden hurdles and on handicap debut at Kilbeggan on latest; can only be watched for now.

Maiden has made a promising start for Harry Kelly; decent third at Clonmel followed by a close second at Tramore (20.5f, good) on latest; nudged up 3lb and stamina to prove at this distance but should go well again.

RaceName: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap
Spotlight: 0-15 but he wasn't discredited when a staying-on third of six in 5f Musselburgh handicap 17 days ago; has his stamina to prove over this markedly longer trip, though.

RaceName: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap
OwnerName: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
Spotlight: A fair 7f juvenile winner; largely running with credit this season and not seen to ideal effect when 12th in 1m Kempton handicap two weeks ago, racing wide; a likely player from a slipping mark for yard among the winners.

RaceName: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to score but has some fair form to her name and she shaped as if the run was needed after three months off when fifth of seven in 7f Chepstow handicap last time; possibilities.

Spotlight: Off the mark over C&D in May and added 1m Leicester victory in July; looked the likely winner until colliding with rail late on when third in 1m2f Brighton handicap last time; big shout off an unchanged mark.

RaceName: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap
Spotlight: Remains winless but he got right back on track with second of ten over C&D two weeks ago; needs to build on that effort if he's to gain a first success at the 12th attempt.

RaceName: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap
Spotlight: A fair 7f scorer last term for Jack Channon; yet to show that form for her new yard this season and beat only one rival at Chepstow (7f) last month; wears first-time hood.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: Won around Sligo last year and handicap winner over this trip at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting; also ran well when third at DRF; 2m6f was too far in the Galway Blazers, but fitter for that and this looks a good opportunity.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: All four chase runs have been at around 2m4f; won novice chase at Punchestown in June; held in pair of handicaps since, beaten 8l at Kilbeggan last time; stiff task at weights, even with 7lb off, and shorter trip no help.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: Winner over hurdles and fences in these colours when with Willie Mullins; poor last of four in last year's renewal; yet to convince with his jumping (can go left), and again made a couple of errors when beaten 20l in Galway handicap on second start for yard.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: Smart handicap hurdler won a big pot at Leopardstown in February; good second on chasing debut at Galway, but well-beaten third behind two good horses at Killarney on Saturday.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: 132-rated hurdler, although only a maiden win to his name, and decent stayer on the Flat as well, third in last season's Cesarewitch; has been hard to place over hurdles, front-running sixth over 2m6f at Galway last time; not bred for this game and stiff task on chasing debut.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Chase
Spotlight: Excels at Cheltenham; first and second in last two runnings of the Grand Annual over 2m; first run since April when well beaten in 2m6f hurdle at Killarney on Saturday, getting tired from two out; best in at the weights if he turns out again, but that must be doubtful.
Thriving for her current yard and bids for a hat-trick after bagging a pair of 6f handicaps at Nottingham and Newmarket; up another 4lb but still merits serious consideration.

Frankel filly who has been off the track since a free-going fourth of eight in 1m Kempton maiden in February; tongue tied for her handicap debut and could still do better now dropping markedly in trip.

Fair maiden who signed off for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole with a good second of six in 7f Brighton handicap in June; changed hands for £8,000 since and not out of things for her new stable after a break.
On the up since sent handicapping and she gained a second win of the summer in 6f handicap at Brighton 19 days ago; remains on a workable mark and very much one to consider.
Winless this season and he came in a below-par sixth of 11 over C&D 11 days ago; more is required if he's to double his tally.
A three-time 5f/6f scorer as a 2yo; on a losing sequence this season and he came in only eighth of 11 over C&D 11 days ago; needs to take a big step forward.
0-8 and she started very slowly when a below-par sixth of ten in 6f Wolverhampton handicap last month; not easy to make a case for.

Remains winless and never able to land a blow in 5f handicaps here and at Newmarket for her new yard this summer; this return to further will suit, though, so she's no forlorn hope with a tongue tie added.

OwnerName: Dr M Voikhansky & Mrs S Voikhanskaya
Spotlight: A fair 7f maiden for Richard Hannon but hasn't offered much in a trio of runs over 7f for her current yard; cheekpieces are reached for here.

Dual winner over hurdles has plenty of chasing experience; after seven months off, nice return to action when third at Wexford; bad mistake early on and nearly lost rider when 11-1 for Galway Blazers, doing well in the circumstances to finish seventh and that race is working out well.
Been a little disappointing over hurdles (now rated 113) and this is no easy task on chasing debut; has King's assistance and half-brother was a chase winner in France.

Half-brother to useful chaser and won sole point; landed two bumpers, including a Leopardstown Grade 2, but went missing for two years until returning this spring; much better on third hurdles run when narrowly beaten over 2m6f in Galway when tongue-tie/cheekpieces combination seemed to perk him up; goes without those aids now on chase debut.
Bumper and 2m4f maiden hurdle winner, but he's not the quickest and has looked laboured over his fences in first two chase starts over 3m1f.
Second in sole point and won heavy-ground maiden hurdle; clear round the priority on this chasing debut after three non-completions over hurdles.
Placed in five of his eight starts over fences, including twice in handicaps and rated 120; lacks a gear but will be plugging away.

Homebred gelding is by Walk In The Park and dam was a Grade-1 winning chaser for Willie Mullins; won 3m maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan last month; promising second to useful sort on chasing debut at Limerick in May; has the build of a chaser and likely to be prominent.
Flat and hurdles winner not coming here in great form; very much Flat-bred and best watched on chasing debut, with yard having stronger contender in Donnie Devito.
Dual winner over hurdles and rated 114 over fences after three solid efforts over shorter; placed on last four visits here, so likely to give a good account and stepping back up in trip is a plus.
Made a winning start for this yard at Leicester (5f) last July but he's offered little in 5f handicaps at Lingfield and Newmarket this summer; others appeal more.
Lightly raced 5yo; yet to hit top form in handicaps here (6f) and at Chepstow (5f) this summer; needs to take a step forward despite a falling mark.
Refused to race here in May but he has since won over C&D and posted a good third of ten in 6f AW Lingfield handicap when hindered by a customary slow start; likely player if on his A-game again.
Landed back-to-back 5f AW handicaps at Lingfield and Chelmsford early in 2026 but she's failed to beat a rival in her last three starts, back on turf at Brighton last time; hard to warm to.
In fine form this summer and bids for a hat-trick following 5f victories at Chepstow and Bath; up 3lb but not taken lightly in her current mood.
On a long losing sequence but recent form includes a couple of encouraging efforts and he did too much up front when fifth of six at Brighton (5f) 19 days ago; needs considering eased 1lb.
Low-mileage 4yo; second run back after 21-month absence when a good third of six in 5f Leicester handicap last month; well in the mix eased 1lb with a hood added.
Off the mark at Yarmouth (5f) in August and didn't enjoy the smoothest of passages when a good third of seven under a 5lb penalty at Brighton (6f) 17 days ago; a player off a 2lb lower mark here.
Scored at Lingfield (6f) in January but below par since, only tenth on a rare turf start at Newmarket (6f) ten days ago; not easy to make a case for.

Spotlight: No Risk At All newcomer bought for E90,000 as 2yo; half-sister to three winners including Excelero (useful 2m-2m2f hurdle/chase) and Kapeloi (French 2m6f Listed chase); dam placed 2m2f hurdle/chase in France, half-sister to French 2m4f/2m6f Grade 1 chase winner Oculi.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Yeats half-sister to yard's winners Friary Road (bumper/2m hurdle), Hardwired (2m1f-2m7f hurdle/chase) and Be Fierce (1m7f chase/2m hurdle); dam bumper (inc Listed) and 2m/2m2f hurdle winner.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Unfancied but showed ability when beaten 15l at Cork last month, finishing fair way off the first three; hood stays on.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Well-bred daughter of Yeats; second of 7 in ordinary Clonmel maiden hurdle in early April; later that month, was beaten 21l against geldings in a valuable sales' bumper at Punchestown; that form untested, but she obviously has a fair measure of ability.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Jukebox Jury newcomer; dam won a bumper and was useful jumper for Jessica Harrington; family of classy chaser In Compliance; tongue-tie.

Spotlight: Half-sister to last month's Galway Blazers winner Kings Hill; 33s, was beaten 27l on debut at Wexford.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Two nice runs and was green under pressure when beaten less than 2l at Sligo last time; drops back in trip from 2m2f

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Nice page; 14-1, keen and didn't finish off when mid-field at Roscommon, but travelled into contention nicely aginst geldings; not far off fifth who won last week; hood should help.
